items.lawSection: New York State Printing and Public Documents Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S983

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the New York state printing and public documents law,
the agriculture and markets law, the environmental conservation law,
the labor law, the mental hygiene law, the social services law, and
the workers' compensation law, in relation to consolidating and
reducing the frequency of reporting requirements and forwarding copies
thereof to the legislative library; and repealing certain provisions
of the labor law, section 2 of chapter 57 of the laws of 1988 amending
the mental hygiene law relating to requiring minimum standards for
active programming of patients at psychiatric centers and reporting on
their development and implementation, section 3 of chapter 762 of the
laws of 1984 amending the education law relating to requiring certain
reports by the state university of New York and the city university of
New York, certain provisions of chapter 166 of the laws of 1991
amending the tax law and other laws relating to deduction or credit by
a shareholder under the article 22 income tax for tax imposed under
article 9-A of the tax law, and certain provisions of the state
university of New York and the city university of New York retirement
incentive act of 1992, relating to the submission and content of
reports and to previously executed provisions of law now obsolete


 PURPOSE :
Consolidates and reduces the frequency of reporting requirements by
various departments, agencies and public authorities; repealer

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This bill amends the environmental conservation law by adding a new
section 54-0102, repeals article 25 of the labor law and adds a new
Article 25, amends subdivision (d) of section 33.03 of the mental
hygiene law by adding new paragraph 3, amends the opening paragraph of
subdivision (d) of section 17 of the social services law is designated
paragraph (i) and a new paragraph (ii) is added, amends subdivision 1
of section 228 of the workers' compensation law, repeals section 3 of
chapter 762 of the laws of 1984, repeals section 357 of chapter 166 of
the laws of 1991, repeals section 11 of chapter 494 of the law of
1992.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Reporting requirements can be one of the Legislature's most effective
tools for monitoring agency operations. Reports can help identify
programs that are not working and can lead to recommendations for
reform. Reports sometimes may not provide the types of information
needed to evaluate program effectiveness. This may be because the
statutory reporting requirements are not specific enough to elicit the
types of needed information to evaluate program effectiveness. Some
reports currently mandated may no longer be needed or not needed as
frequently.

This bill provides mandate relief through the elimination of unneeded
reporting requirements and reduced frequency of other requirements,
and improves government accountability through strengthened reporting
requirements. It does this by eliminating, reducing the frequency, and
strengthening certain reports. The Oversight Committee completed a
telephone survey of twenty-three agencies in an attempt to discern
agencies' distribution policies for statutorily required reports
issued to the "legislature."

The results of the survey indicated that how agencies interpreted the
"legislature" varied dependent upon a.number of variables including,
but not limited to, the nature of the report, the degree of public
interest or controversy associated with the report and the financial
situation of the reporting agencies. Eight agencies indicated that
they interpreted reports to the legislature to mean each and every
member of the legislature is to receive a full copy of the report at
all times. Other agencies felt that they satisfied the requirements of
statute by providing reports to selected members. To deal with this
the bill creates a consistent policy for the handling of the
distribution of reports to the legislature. It also provides for an
executive summary which will highlight the provisions of the reports
including, as appropriate, findings and recommendations.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Possible cost reduction.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately, provided, however, section
54-0102 of the environmental conservation law, as added by section
four of this act, shall take effect on the first January next
succeeding the date on which this act shall have become law.
